title: etbb-july-2024-may-2025-update.pdf — section 702
text:
510 For example, see Re A (Children) (Remote Hearing: Care and Placement Orders) [2020] EWCA Civ 583.
Remote hearings
Equal Treatment Bench Book – July 2024 (May 2025 update) 322
• Introduce everyone in the “room”. Explain how and when they will appear on screen. This
is particularly important to reduce anxiety for people with certain mental impairments or
neurodiverse conditions.
• Provide reassurance about technology. Check everyone can clearly hear and see what is
happening. Just because the judge’s own reception is satisfactory, or the judge can
follow events where reception is poor, does not mean that others feel comfortable.
• Tell everyone that they must immediately say if they experience any loss of reception,
and they should not feel embarrassed or inhibited. Explain the risk of the IT failing
altogether and what should be done if the link fails.
